title: Conjugation formulas for triple compositor and both unit pastings across equivalences
statement:
Let $\mathcal I$ be a category. For every object $i$ let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ be categories and $E_i:\mathcal A_i\simeq\mathcal B_i$ an equivalence, in particular fully faithful in the Hom-set sense of [def-sf-induced-category]. For every arrow $a:i\to j$, specify functors $F_a:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$, $G_a:\mathcal B_i\to\mathcal B_j$ and a natural isomorphism $a_a:E_jF_a\cong G_aE_i$. For composable $a:i\to j$, $b:j\to k$, specify natural isomorphisms $\kappa_{b,a}:F_{ba}\cong F_bF_a$ and $\bar\kappa_{b,a}:G_{ba}\cong G_bG_a$. Specify also $\epsilon_i:F_{1_i}\cong1_{\mathcal A_i}$ and $\bar\epsilon_i:G_{1_i}\cong1_{\mathcal B_i}$. Composition notation is functional, so $ba=b\circ a$. Neither associativity nor unit coherence of these data is assumed. All expressions below include the canonical functor associators and unitors and the transports along associativity and identity equalities in $\mathcal I$.

Put $b_{b,a}=(G_ba_a)\circ(a_bF_a)$, and assume the pair and identity comparison squares
$$b_{b,a}\circ(E_k\kappa_{b,a})=(\bar\kappa_{b,a}E_i)\circ a_{ba},\qquad E_i\epsilon_i=(\bar\epsilon_iE_i)\circ a_{1_i}.$$
For every triple $i\xrightarrow a j\xrightarrow b k\xrightarrow c l$, put
$$L=(F_c\kappa_{b,a})\circ\kappa_{c,ba},\quad P=(\kappa_{c,b}F_a)\circ\kappa_{cb,a},$$
and define $\bar L,\bar P$ by replacing $F,\kappa$ with $G,\bar\kappa$. Let
$$B_{c,b,a}=(G_cG_ba_a)\circ(G_ca_bF_a)\circ(a_cF_bF_a):E_lF_cF_bF_a\cong G_cG_bG_aE_i.$$
Then the two explicit pasting identities are
$$E_lL=B_{c,b,a}^{-1}\circ(\bar L E_i)\circ a_{cba},\qquad E_lP=B_{c,b,a}^{-1}\circ(\bar P E_i)\circ a_{cba}.$$
For an arrow $a:i\to j$, put $U_a=(\epsilon_jF_a)\circ\kappa_{1_j,a}$ and $V_a=(F_a\epsilon_i)\circ\kappa_{a,1_i}$, interpreted as endomorphisms of $F_a$ using the specified equality transports; define $\bar U_a,\bar V_a$ analogously. Both unit pasting identities are
$$E_jU_a=a_a^{-1}\circ(\bar U_aE_i)\circ a_a,\qquad E_jV_a=a_a^{-1}\circ(\bar V_aE_i)\circ a_a.$$
Consequently if $\bar L=\bar P$, $\bar U_a=1_{G_a}$ and $\bar V_a=1_{G_a}$, then $L=P$, $U_a=1_{F_a}$ and $V_a=1_{F_a}$. The formulas apply without making any $E_i$ or $a_a$ an identity.

proof.text: Work componentwise, writing $\alpha_d(x)=(a_d)_x$, and write juxtaposition of morphisms for functional composition (rightmost first). Thus $E_lL_x$ means $E_l(L_x)$. A natural transformation $t:H\Rightarrow K$ satisfies $K(f)t_x=t_yH(f)$; this is its defining naturality equation. The canonical associators and unitors for composition of ordinary functors have identity components. Expand them before taking components. Likewise, for the stated transports along equalities of arrows in $\mathcal I$, substitute the equal arrows in the indexed data; both paths then have the same indices. The calculations below therefore prove the formulas with their specified associators, unitors and equality transports, without any coherence assumption on $\kappa$ or $\epsilon$.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 1 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
For the left triple pasting fix $x\in\mathcal A_i$. Naturality of $a_c:E_lF_c\cong G_cE_k$ at $\kappa_{b,a}(x):F_{ba}x\to F_bF_ax$ says
$$\alpha_c(F_bF_ax)E_l(F_c(\kappa_{b,a}(x)))=G_c(E_k(\kappa_{b,a}(x)))\alpha_c(F_{ba}x).$$
Expand $B_xE_l(L_x)$ and substitute this equality. Functoriality of $G_c$ gives
$$B_xE_l(L_x)=G_c\!\left(G_b(\alpha_a(x))\alpha_b(F_ax)E_k(\kappa_{b,a}(x))\right)\alpha_c(F_{ba}x)E_l(\kappa_{c,ba}(x)).$$
This is only the defining naturality equation followed by reassociation of morphisms.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 2 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
Apply the assumed pair square for $(b,a)$ at $x$ to the parenthesized expression in step 2: it is $\bar\kappa_{b,a}(E_ix)\alpha_{ba}(x)$. Consequently
$$B_xE_l(L_x)=G_c(\bar\kappa_{b,a}(E_ix))G_c(\alpha_{ba}(x))\alpha_c(F_{ba}x)E_l(\kappa_{c,ba}(x)).$$
The last three factors are the pair square for $(c,ba)$ at $x$, so this equals
$$G_c(\bar\kappa_{b,a}(E_ix))\bar\kappa_{c,ba}(E_ix)\alpha_{cba}(x)=\bar L_{E_ix}\alpha_{cba}(x).$$
Here $(c,ba)$ is composable, so both squares used are among the hypotheses.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 3 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
For the right triple pasting, expand its components as
$$B_xE_l(P_x)=G_cG_b(\alpha_a(x))G_c(\alpha_b(F_ax))\alpha_c(F_bF_ax)E_l(\kappa_{c,b}(F_ax))E_l(\kappa_{cb,a}(x)).$$
The pair square for $(c,b)$, evaluated at the object $F_ax\in\mathcal A_j$, replaces the middle three factors by $\bar\kappa_{c,b}(E_jF_ax)\alpha_{cb}(F_ax)$. Hence
$$B_xE_l(P_x)=G_cG_b(\alpha_a(x))\bar\kappa_{c,b}(E_jF_ax)\alpha_{cb}(F_ax)E_l(\kappa_{cb,a}(x)).$$

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 4 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
Naturality of $\bar\kappa_{c,b}:G_{cb}\cong G_cG_b$ at $\alpha_a(x):E_jF_ax\to G_aE_ix$ gives
$$G_cG_b(\alpha_a(x))\bar\kappa_{c,b}(E_jF_ax)=\bar\kappa_{c,b}(G_aE_ix)G_{cb}(\alpha_a(x)).$$
Use this in step 4 and then the assumed pair square for $(cb,a)$ at $x$. The result is
$$B_xE_l(P_x)=\bar\kappa_{c,b}(G_aE_ix)\bar\kappa_{cb,a}(E_ix)\alpha_{cba}(x)=\bar P_{E_ix}\alpha_{cba}(x).$$
The naturality input is a morphism in $\mathcal B_j$, exactly the source category of $\bar\kappa_{c,b}$.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 5 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
Each $B_x$ is invertible, being a composite of components of natural isomorphisms and their functor images. Multiply the equalities in steps 3 and 5 on the left by $B_x^{-1}$. This gives
$$E_l(L_x)=B_x^{-1}\bar L_{E_ix}\alpha_{cba}(x),\qquad E_l(P_x)=B_x^{-1}\bar P_{E_ix}\alpha_{cba}(x).$$
Equality of natural transformations is componentwise equality; equality of natural isomorphisms follows from equality of their forward maps, since inverses are unique. These are the two asserted triple formulas.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 6 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
For the left unit, the identity square at the object $F_ax$ gives $E_j(\epsilon_j(F_ax))=\bar\epsilon_j(E_jF_ax)\alpha_{1_j}(F_ax)$. Naturality of $\bar\epsilon_j:G_{1_j}\cong1_{\mathcal B_j}$ at $\alpha_a(x)$ gives $\alpha_a(x)\bar\epsilon_j(E_jF_ax)=\bar\epsilon_j(G_aE_ix)G_{1_j}(\alpha_a(x))$. Substituting these two equations yields
$$\alpha_a(x)E_j(U_{a,x})=\bar\epsilon_j(G_aE_ix)G_{1_j}(\alpha_a(x))\alpha_{1_j}(F_ax)E_j(\kappa_{1_j,a}(x)).$$
Use the pair square for $(1_j,a)$ in the last three factors and substitute $1_ja=a$. The expression becomes $\bar\epsilon_j(G_aE_ix)\bar\kappa_{1_j,a}(E_ix)\alpha_a(x)=\bar U_{a,E_ix}\alpha_a(x)$.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 7 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
For the right unit, naturality of $a_a$ at $\epsilon_i(x):F_{1_i}x\to x$ gives $\alpha_a(x)E_j(F_a(\epsilon_i(x)))=G_a(E_i(\epsilon_i(x)))\alpha_a(F_{1_i}x)$. Substitute this and then the identity square $E_i(\epsilon_i(x))=\bar\epsilon_i(E_ix)\alpha_{1_i}(x)$ to obtain
$$\alpha_a(x)E_j(V_{a,x})=G_a(\bar\epsilon_i(E_ix))G_a(\alpha_{1_i}(x))\alpha_a(F_{1_i}x)E_j(\kappa_{a,1_i}(x)).$$
The pair square for $(a,1_i)$ replaces the last three factors by $\bar\kappa_{a,1_i}(E_ix)\alpha_a(x)$ after the substitution $a1_i=a$. The result is $G_a(\bar\epsilon_i(E_ix))\bar\kappa_{a,1_i}(E_ix)\alpha_a(x)=\bar V_{a,E_ix}\alpha_a(x)$.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 8 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text:
Multiply the identities in steps 7 and 8 on the left by $\alpha_a(x)^{-1}$. Componentwise equality now gives
$$E_jU_a=a_a^{-1}(\bar U_aE_i)a_a,\qquad E_jV_a=a_a^{-1}(\bar V_aE_i)a_a.$$
This proves both unit formulas for the specified, possibly nonidentity $a_a$; no replacement of $E_i$ or $a_a$ by identity data has occurred.

source.place: Refinement isomorphisms and cocycle paragraph; agent-written component calculation, step 9 (formal equivalence transport underlying the returned parent steps 4–5).

proof.text: If $\bar L=\bar P$, the triple formulas imply $E_l(L_x)=E_l(P_x)$ for every $x$. Full faithfulness in [def-sf-induced-category] means precisely that the map on each Hom set is bijective, hence injective, so $L_x=P_x$. Thus $L=P$. If $\bar U_a=1$ and $\bar V_a=1$, the two unit formulas and inverse cancellation give $E_j(U_{a,x})=1_{E_jF_ax}=E_j(1_{F_ax})$ and $E_j(V_{a,x})=E_j(1_{F_ax})$. Injectivity on these Hom sets gives $U_{a,x}=1_{F_ax}=V_{a,x}$; componentwise equality proves both remaining conclusions. Only the injective part of the stated full faithfulness is used.
